subject: Why can't you use an output more than once, please?

messages.author: 2a8df5fc9d8b8366
messages.subject: Why can't you use an output more than once, please?
parts:
Hello,

Would someone please let me know why you cannot use an output element more than once, please?

Using the Shiny "census-app" as an example, why is it that using "text2" is only allowed once, please?  Why does that element disappear after use?

server.R
shinyServer(function(input, output) {

     output$text1 <- renderText({ 
          paste("You have selected", input$var)
     })
 
output$text2 <- renderText({ 
          paste("You have chosen a range that goes from ",input$range[1]," to ", input$range[2])
     })

  }
)

ui.R
shinyUI(fluidPage(
  titlePanel("censusVis"),
  
  sidebarLayout(
    sidebarPanel(
      helpText("Create demographic maps with 
        information from the 2010 US Census."),
      
      selectInput("var", 
        label = "Choose a variable to display",
        choices = c("Percent White", "Percent Black",
          "Percent Hispanic", "Percent Asian"),
        selected = "Percent White"),
      
      sliderInput("range", 
        label = "Range of interest:",
        min = 0, max = 100, value = c(0, 100))
    ),
    
    mainPanel(
      textOutput("text1"),
 br(),
 textOutput("text2"),
 br(),
 
          # App will not run because of this second use of "text2"
          textOutput("text2"),
)
  )
))



Thank you,
Jo

messages.author: ca443e6eaa0e78ed
messages.subject: Re: Why can't you use an output more than once, please?
parts:
There are classes of outputs that can't be represented twice in the same page. For example, renderPlot by default will use the width of the output to determine what size to render the plot at; if there were multiple outputs then that wouldn't work.

And from an implementation perspective, we map these output IDs to HTML element IDs, and HTML element IDs must be unique.

parts:
Joe: Re-using inputs and outputs would still be convenient. Especially in larger applications with many pages and menu's that are using the same data and variables. Throwing an error if you do reuse one by accident could also be helpful :)

Would it be possible to have something like an OO class of object and either (1) create an instance of that object that is independent or (2) a copy but with a unique id that is automatically dependent on other instances?
